user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: MIL-to-mask self-distillation with cross-level agreement
SUMMARY: First train the segmentation adapters with the problem's top-k MIL, then convert their multi-level maps on abnormal source images into pseudo-masks (patches anomalous at three or more levels) and retrain with MVFA's Dice and Focal losses on those pseudo-masks.
HYPOTHESIS: One round of MIL-to-mask self-distillation increases held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over MIL alone, and cross-level agreement (>= 3 levels) yields pseudo-masks with at least 1.5x the precision of deepest-level pseudo-masks.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: segmentation supervision (true masks; top-k MIL only; MIL followed by one or two rounds of pseudo-mask self-distillation). Round 0: top-k MIL (k = 1%) on all source images. Pseudo-mask of an abnormal source image: patches in the image-wise top 5% at >= 3 of the 4 levels, upsampled with nearest neighbour; normal images get empty masks; pixels of abnormal images outside the pseudo-mask but above the image median are ignored in the Focal term. Rounds 1-2: Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities; pseudo-mask precision and recall against true masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC source images (analysis only).
RATIONALE: MIL supervises only the top patches and gives fragmented maps, but its maps on abnormal source images contain coarse localisation. Turning the MIL-trained maps into pseudo-masks with cross-level agreement and training the segmentation adapters on them with MVFA's own Dice and Focal losses (self-distillation) can densify the supervision while still never using an expert mask.
METHOD: 1) Round 0 as in the problem statement (loss.py: topk_mil). 2) New script make_pseudo_masks.py: run the round-0 seg branch on all source training images, compute per-level probability maps, apply the agreement rule, save masks and ignore maps as .npy. 3) dataset/medical_zero.py: load pseudo-masks for every source dataset (seg_idx >= 0 for all six). 4) train_zero.py round 1: existing Focal + Dice with an ignore weight map. 5) Optional round 2 regenerates pseudo-masks from the round-1 model. Hyper-parameters: top 5%, agreement >= 3 levels, released learning rate and epochs per round.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL only. Ablations: agreement threshold (2, 3, 4 levels); top percentage (2%, 5%, 10%); number of rounds. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over MIL only.

Idea B:
TITLE: Cross-level consensus MIL: choosing instances by agreement of the four adapter levels
SUMMARY: Select the positive instances of an abnormal image as the patches on which all four segmentation levels agree (geometric mean of level probabilities) and apply the MIL loss to those patches at every level, in a single training stage.
HYPOTHESIS: Training MVFA's segmentation adapters with consensus MIL — top-k (k = 1%) selected on the geometric mean of the four level maps rather than per level — raises held-out pixel AUROC by at least 2 points and AUPRO by at least 3 points over per-level top-k MIL, because single-level top-k selections disagree and each level reinforces its own spurious maxima.
RATIONALE: The self-distillation parent shows that cross-level agreement filters noisy evidence, but uses it only after training, in a second stage that can lock in errors. The anchor-frame parent shows that all four levels read their patches in the same fixed anchor frame, so their probabilities are directly comparable across levels. Together they suggest a different mechanism: use cross-level agreement inside the MIL loss itself, as the instance selector. Per-level top-k lets each level pick its own (often anatomical) maxima; a consensus selector picks only patches that every level finds anomalous, which are more likely to be lesions, and then trains every level on those patches. This is one-stage, needs no pseudo-masks, and is a direct modification of the problem's operator.
METHOD: 1) loss.py: consensus_mil(p_levels, label, k_frac=0.01): c = exp(mean_l log p_l) per patch; idx = topk(c); positive loss for abnormal images = mean over levels of BCE(mean(p_l[idx]), 1); normal images: BCE(top-k mean of p_l, 0) per level as in the problem. 2) train_zero.py: replace the problem's per-level top-k MIL with consensus_mil; selection indices are detached. 3) Hyper-parameters: k_frac {0.5%, 1%, 2%}; consensus by geometric mean (ablation: minimum over levels); released learning rate and epochs. 4) Inference unchanged.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Ablations: geometric mean vs. minimum; consensus over levels 2-4 only. Diagnostics: overlap of per-level top-k selections; fraction of selected patches inside true masks on masked source images. Falsified if consensus MIL does not beat per-level MIL in AUPRO.
